most_relevant.description: What an incredible place full of history. I suggest taking a tour to get the most out of your visit. We didn't reserve a tour before we arrived but found an English speaking tour guide willing to show us around at the entrance. Hearing the stories of the "residents" and the history of the cemetery made our visit so much richer.

A surprisingly fascinating place to visit. This cemetery is the real deal, with beautiful architecture and plenty of history. Just remember to be respectful… and maybe save the midnight adventures for somewhere else.

Well worth the visit. This is a beautiful urban cemetery with many famous persons interred here. This cemetery rivals Pere Lachaise and beats any New Orleans cemetery for beauty. The range of architectural styles and the cleanliness makes this place unique. Eva Peron and most famous Argentinians are buried here.

A really interesting place to visit, the graves are so ornate and beautiful to see. It is crazy how much people pay for these but shows how much they care about family! I would highly recommend paying for a tour guide as the stories are worth hearing, as well as fully understanding who the graves are for.
It’s amazing! Wow, these tombs are incredible. Easy to spend an hour wandering around. You get a map with your ticket, locating the prominent mausoleums. $24 USD to enter

A visually stunning and expansive cemetery in Buenos Aires. The sheer scale is impressive and the elaborate detail on the massive, ornate mausoleums is incredible. It’s like walking through an outdoor museum of art and history. You could easily spend hours exploring and walking the cemetery. However, at $17 USD for foreign visitors, it felt overpriced. It’s a very cool experience and I personally thought it was worth seeing, but the high entry fee for foreigners keeps this from being a must see attraction that I would recommend to anyone.

A fascinating open-air museum in the heart of Buenos Aires. Established in 1822, this historic cemetery is famous for its stunning architecture and marble mausoleums. It is the final resting place of many influential figures, including Eva Perón (Evita). A visit here is a must for anyone traveling to Buenos Aires to appreciate the history, art, and peaceful atmosphere of this iconic landmark.

We went with a Trip Advisor walking tour, and it was absolutely fantastic. The history in this place and stories that live on here are well worth an afternoon visit. From past presidents to athletes to celebrities, they rest here in peace. Highly recommended.
